title: observability: refine token-level KV metrics, logging, tracing, dashboards and alert thresholds
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: token-level KV metrics and associated dashboards/alerts have accumulated drift after recent batching and KV caching changes (ENG-8942, ENG-9021). This PR consolidates token-level metrics, reduces high-cardinality tracing tags, refines Grafana panels for cost/latency breakdowns, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce noisy incidents. Changes include instrumentation updates (new histograms for token latency, per-model token cost counters, KV cache hit/miss counters aggregated by model+route), tracing improvements (sample-by-error and hash session_id to avoid high-cardinality), logging changes (structured token-level logs behind a feature flag, redact PII), dashboard updates (layout, sensible defaults for time ranges and grouping by model family), and alert rule adjustments (longer evaluation windows for token-cost spikes, higher thresholds for transient latency spikes). Motivation: reduce alert noise, improve SRE signal-to-noise, and provide clearer unit economics per token and route for product teams. Checklist: add/updated metrics collectors and exporters; update Grafana dashboard JSON and add panel descriptions; migrate existing alerts to new metric names with compat shim; add unit tests for metrics aggregation; run integration tests in staging; documentation updates in docs/observability. Backwards compatibility: compat shim emits old metric names for 30 days; migration notes added in docs. Impact: expected to reduce alert noise for token-cost spikes by ~60% and make regressions easier to investigate via token-level breakdowns.
